result.summary: Converts `building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` from an eagerly evaluated variable into a procedure evaluated when lowering derivations. This ensures cross-toolchain packages use the target system passed via Guix's `--system` flag rather than the host system running `guix shell`.
result.problem: When running Guix with `--system` under emulation on a host of a different architecture (for example, `--system=aarch64-linux` on an x86_64 host), `guix shell` loads manifests before applying `--system`. As a result, `building-on` captures the host's `%current-system`, causing cross toolchains like `gcc-cross-sans-libc` to configure with mismatched `--build` triplets and fail to build.
evidence: PR description demonstrates build failure: 'checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet' when building under `--system=aarch64-linux` on x86_64
PR description confirms native builds produce identical toolchain derivations to master on both `linux_static.scm` and `manifest_gui.scm`
result.changed_since_previous: No functional changes; the previous description was generated before the patch was available.
result.card: Converts the `building-on` triplet resolution in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` from an eagerly evaluated variable into a procedure evaluated when lowering derivations. When running Guix with `--system` on a foreign host via emulation (such as building for aarch64 on x86_64), manifests previously evaluated `%current-system` at module load time, generating an incorrect `--build` triplet that broke cross-toolchain configuration for `gcc-cross-sans-libc`. The change fixes emulated cross-system Guix builds without modifying the derivations produced for native release builds.

risk.why: A mistake in Guix toolchain definitions could alter compiler build flags or break reproducible release builds across supported architectures.
